claim: The surface becomes an old CRT — barrel-curved glass, drifting scanlines, and a slow rolling flicker band — retro phosphor warmth over the real content (content still readable through the curve).

q1_defects.answer: One genuinely dead control and weak/absent headline motion; no placeholder-slab, no clipping, no broken frame. The 'scanlines' frequency knob (40->220) produces zero visible change at native resolution.
evidence: metrics: scanlines control changed=false meanAbsDiff=0.122 changedFrac=0
crt-warp/after/control-scanlines-low.png vs crt-warp/after/control-scanlines-high.png — visually indistinguishable line density
metrics: rollSpeed control changed=false meanAbsDiff=0.049 changedFrac=0
metrics: play-1/2/3 frameDeltaMag=0.08/0.10/0.11 — near-static, no visible rolling band drift

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes at meaningful curvature — it reads convincingly as a CRT barrel-curved glass with scanline ridges and phosphor bloom over the REAL card content. Premium-adjacent; the default-state bulge is a touch subtle.
evidence: crt-warp/after/control-curvature-high.png — strong fish-eye barrel bulge, rounded bezel, content wraps the curve = unmistakable CRT glass
crt-warp/after/control-scanStrength-high.png — fine horizontal scanline ridges across the curved body = phosphor tube read
crt-warp/after/play-2.png — amber header, grey rows, blue accent dot all preserved and curved (real card distorted, not a slab)

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. The card already shows a soft barrel outline and specular bloom at idle, inviting the effect; sweeping curvature makes the CRT bulge obvious and satisfying.
evidence: crt-warp/after/idle.png — card shows subtle barrel-curved edges + corner bloom even at rest
crt-warp/after/control-curvature-low.png — flat crisp card baseline makes the bulge in -high read as a deliberate transformation

q4_responsive.answer: Partially. curvature is strongly live and scanStrength is visibly live; but scanlines is dead and rollSpeed shows no change in the static capture.
evidence: crt-warp/after/control-curvature-low.png (flat) vs crt-warp/after/control-curvature-high.png (deep barrel) — strong live change, metrics meanAbsDiff=5.178 changedFrac=0.1
crt-warp/after/control-scanStrength-low.png vs crt-warp/after/control-scanStrength-high.png — scanline ridges clearly more prominent at high
metrics: scanlines changed=false meanAbsDiff=0.122 — DEAD frequency knob
metrics: rollSpeed changed=false meanAbsDiff=0.049 — no visible change in frozen capture

q5_net.answer: Leaning positive on the core effect but blocked by a dead control: the barrel curve is genuine and the real card is preserved, but a user who grabs the scanlines knob gets nothing, and the promised drifting/rolling motion is not visible in the play sequence.
evidence: crt-warp/after/control-curvature-high.png — the strong, satisfying CRT bulge is the win
metrics: scanlines changed=false; play frameDeltaMag<=0.11 — the dead knob and absent roll band are the letdowns

mustFix.issue: 'scanlines' control (line frequency 40->220) is dead — a user dragging it sees zero change in line density, which is an objectively broken control on a CRT effect whose whole identity is scanlines.
mustFix.evidence: metrics: scanlines changed=false meanAbsDiff=0.122 changedFrac=0; crt-warp/after/control-scanlines-low.png vs control-scanlines-high.png are visually indistinguishable

flags.note: Headline 'drifting scanlines / slow rolling flicker band' motion is not visible across the play sequence (near-static). May be the cosine sweep pinning near-static phases, but a driving user would expect to see the band travel.
flags.evidence: metrics: play-1/2/3 frameDeltaMag=0.08/0.10/0.11; crt-warp/after/play-1.png vs play-2.png vs play-3.png are near-identical

flags.note: 'rollSpeed' shows no change in the frozen capture; expected for a speed knob (manifests only over time), but it leaves two of four controls without verifiable live behavior in the evidence.
flags.evidence: metrics: rollSpeed changed=false meanAbsDiff=0.049; crt-warp/after/control-rollSpeed-low.png vs control-rollSpeed-high.png indistinguishable

flags.note: Default-state curvature is a touch subtle vs the dramatic -high sweep; bumping the default bulge would read more premium out of the box.
